cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he opens by calling on the heavenly beings. Friend, most of us can't even get the group chat to answer back. David's calling up HEAVEN. And he's got something he wants them to give the LORD.

cards.question: What does David call on the heavenly beings to ascribe to the LORD?
David keeps going with the heavenly beings. True or false: he says glory is due to the LORD's name.

cards.text: Then the whole psalm turns into a storm, and the voice of the LORD is over the waters. Not a little drizzle, friend. MANY waters.

cards.question: In this storm over the waters, the God of glory ___.
After all that thunder over the waters, how does David describe the voice of the LORD?

cards.text: Next, the voice of the LORD reaches Lebanon. And Lebanon has TREES, friend. Tall, thick, been-standing-there-forever trees. The kind that don't move for anybody.

cards.question: Up in Lebanon, the voice of the LORD ___ the cedars.

cards.text: Then He makes Lebanon skip like a calf, and Sirion, another name for Mount Hermon (Deut 3:9), skip like a young wild ox. Mountains SKIPPING. Me? I need a running start just to hop my gold base over a chocolate chip.

cards.question: Thunder, broken cedars, skipping mountains. Now the voice of the LORD strikes with something else. What?
The voice of the LORD shakes the wilderness too. Which wilderness does David name?

cards.text: The voice of the LORD twists the oaks and strips the forests bare. And I used to think a little dust falling in the junk drawer was a rough day. Then the scene cuts from the storm to His temple.

cards.question: While the storm rages, what goes up in His temple? In His temple all cry, “___!”

cards.text: Waters, fire, shaking ground. Now David shows us where the LORD is through ALL of it. And no, He's not hiding under the counter like I would be.

cards.question: With that storm going on, where does David say the LORD sits?
True or false: David says the LORD is King only until the storm is over.
At the start, David called on the heavenly beings to ascribe strength to the LORD. True or false: at the end, the LORD gives strength to the heavenly beings.
After all that thunder, the last line goes to His people. The LORD blesses His people with ___.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: 'This is a psalm of David...', 'Friend, most of us can't even get the group chat to answer back.', 'David's calling up HEAVEN.' and 'And he's got something he wants them to give the LORD.'

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Psalm 29:2b, 'worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness', is never told on any card. The walkthrough goes straight from the glory due His name to the voice over the waters, so the psalm's call to worship is missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question says the temple cry happens 'While the storm rages.' Psalm 29:9 only says 'And in His temple all cry, “Glory!”' and gives no time for it. The text leaves open how the cry connects to the voice of the LORD in the forests.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The question 'With that storm going on, where does David say the LORD sits?' ties 'the flood' of Psalm 29:10 to the storm in verses 3 to 9 and makes the two happen at the same time. The text doesn't say how the flood connects to the storm.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
